Small | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a double-shelled hollow Na3V2(PO4)2F3/Na3V2(PO4)3 heterostructure, where the outer shell buffers volume changes and suppresses fluorine loss, enabling stable multielectron V4+/V5+ redox. Significance: it delivers 131.7 mAh g−1, 471 Wh kg−1, and 78.8% retention after 1000 cycles, offering a strategy for high-energy, long-life sodium-ion batteries.

The work clarifies cation-doping regulation of local bonding, offering design guidance for high-performance halide solid electrolytes.

ENERGY & ENVIRONMENTAL MATERIALS | ⭐ Review | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This review uniquely integrates atomic-scale characterization insights into O3/O1 stacking evolution, surface/interfacial degradation, and phase deterioration of high-Ni cathodes, while comparing single- versus polycrystalline degradation behaviors including stress–strain and cracking. It critically assesses modification strategies reinforcing intrinsic structural stability, offering rational design guidelines for high-voltage, high-energy-density cathodes in next-generation Li-ion batteries.
